question_text: Choose the sentence that adheres to standard Civil Service English grammar rules.

options.text: The committee have decided to postpone the administrative hearing.
Neither the supervisor nor the employees was aware of the memo.
Neither the supervisor nor the employees were aware of the memo.
The list of approved applicants were posted on the bulletin board.

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang Tunay na Subject
hint_ladder.text: Sa bawat pangungusap, tanungin mo: sino o ano talaga ang gumagawa ng aksyon? Huwag magpalinlang sa extra words.

hint_ladder.title: Ang Rule sa 'Neither/Nor'
hint_ladder.text: Kapag may 'neither...nor' o 'either...or', tandaan: ang verb dapat tugma sa subject na pinakamalapit. Yung unang subject, dedma muna.

hint_ladder.title: Subukan ang Pinakamalapit na Subject
hint_ladder.text: Sa B at C, ang pinakamalapit na subject sa verb ay 'employees' (plural). Kaya dapat plural din ang verb—'were', hindi 'was'.

hint_ladder.title: Hulihin ang mga Mapanlinlang na Salita
hint_ladder.text: Sa ibang pangungusap: A—'committee' ay iisang grupo, D—'list' singular kahit may 'of applicants'. Iisang sagot lang ang sumusunod sa lahat ng rules.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'committee' seems plural, but it's a single unit needing 'has'.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'supervisor' is singular, but 'employees' is nearer, so 'were' is needed.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'applicants' is plural and close, but the real subject is 'list', needing 'was'.

next_time_rule: Sa 'neither/nor' o 'either/or', ang verb sumusunod sa pinakamalapit na subject. Also, ingat sa phrases na sumisingit, gaya ng 'of the applicants'.
blueprint_id: Subject-Verb Agreement — Proximity Rule with Neither/Nor
deconstruct_text:
Let’s analyze using a typical barangay hall scenario. The Lupon Tagapamayapa committee (a single body) has decided on a case schedule. So 'has decided' is correct, not 'have decided'.

Now, imagine the City Administrator and employees did not know about a new memo. Applying the 'neither...nor' rule: the verb agrees with the subject nearest it. Since 'employees' is plural and closer, we say 'were aware', not 'was aware'.

Hence B is wrong, C is correct. For D, picture a bulletin board at your LGU listing approved applicants. The real subject is 'list', not 'applicants'. The phrase 'of approved applicants' is just a description. So 'was posted' is right.

Only C follows all rules. Taglish memory hook: Kapag 'neither/nor', isipin mo yung katabi ng verb—siya lang ang pinapansin, yung isa deadma na. At 'yung mga 'of' phrases, laging check sino talaga ang boss na subject.
